questions.prompt: Why is resilience not a fixed personal trait in this lesson?
questions.answer: Adaptation varies across contexts, time, resources and domains.
questions.feedback: Distinguish a trajectory from a label.

questions.prompt: Give one resource beyond the individual.
questions.answer: Social support, accessible services, secure housing or institutional flexibility.
questions.feedback: Explain its relevance to the challenge.

questions.prompt: Does emotional distress rule out adaptation?
questions.answer: No; distress and functioning may coexist or change differently.
Changing harmful conditions may support adaptation more directly than asking individuals to endure them.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer, formative only; use specific feedback and delayed retest.
scoring.practice: Describes adaptation in context, distinguishes resources from outcomes and identifies structural as well as personal support.
scoring.transfer: Create an adversity-resource map for a novel fictional disruption. Include at least one resource at three different levels and a modest functional objective. Explain why the objective cannot serve as a universal resilience score.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; never average away missing or safety-critical evidence. Quizzes cannot certify competence.
